audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart calls levels 1-5 a coin flip, gives Locke level 6 and first item, and calls the 2-item stage even — the content layer says the exact opposite at every row.
audit.why: whys[0] to whys[3] each state Fiora owns that level outright, whys[4] and whys[5] call 6 and first item even, whys[6] says two-plus items are Fiora's. packet.levelChart is Fiora, Fiora, Fiora, Fiora, Skill, Skill, Fiora — an exact match.
audit.corrected: win[0..3] and phases[0..3] -> Fiora; win[4], win[5] and phases[4], phases[5] -> Skill; win[6]/phases[6] -> Fiora, with ratings aligned.

audit.whatIsWrong: The 'ten seconds' figure for his blink is stated as prose folklore with no ability cooldowns given for Purgatory or the nails.
audit.why: Ashen Pursuit is a flat 10s at every rank — the ten-second window is real and worth naming as a cooldown; Purgatory is 120/100/80; Ritual Nails is 10/9/8/7/6; Soul Ignition 18/17/16/15/14.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and dosFull[2].d now carry the flat 10s E and the 120s R.

audit.whatIsWrong: Purgatory GROUNDS, and nothing on the page says so. That is the single most important interaction in this matchup: inside the zone Fiora's Lunge — her engage, her disengage and her Vital-chasing tool — does not work. The page only warns about the execute threshold.
audit.why: enemyKit R flags grounding ('shuts off enemy dashes') alongside execute, slow and zone; Fiora's Q is flagged 'mobility that grounding and walls can deny'. Also: report[8] calls anti-heal optional because his sustain is 'self-refund', but Grievous Wounds reduces self-healing too, so it does cut Soul Ignition's refund.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns and dontsFull[0].d now state the grounding; report[8] corrected on Grievous Wounds.

Track it before every step-up. - Locke E (Ashen Pursuit): his ONLY mobility, resets on takedowns — the post-E window is the lane. - Locke R (Purgatory): never fight at sliver HP inside the zone.
edits.after: - Locke Ritual Nails (Marks): matchup-defining — the marks are his whole engine; without 2-3 stacks on you his blink-in barely dents, so sidestep the recasts. - Locke E (Ashen Pursuit): a flat 10s, his ONLY mobility, resets on takedowns — the post-E window is the lane. - Locke R (Purgatory): 120s, and it GROUNDS — your Lunge is dead inside the zone, so never fight at sliver HP in it.

notes: Locke's Purgatory grounding is the decisive fact in this matchup and was absent from all 30+ writable fields — worth surfacing on the page body, not just the do/don't list. wants.you[0..2] and wants.foe[0..2] are all under 25 characters, so the applier skips them; they are unusably terse ("Survive to level 6") and want a manual rewrite. Q's display name 'Ritual Nails' could not be confirmed from the kit file — Riot's text only says he 'readies a set of Soul Nails to throw', and the packet carried no enemyAbilities block for this champion, so I left every occurrence alone.
